subject: turtle
pitch: A green sea turtle gliding through the water. A heart-shaped shell with olive and caramel plates traced in darker brown, a pale yellow belly plate, a blunt head with cream-edged scales, dark wise eyes and a gentle beak. Long front flippers spread wide, short rear flippers, and a little remora fish riding under its shell.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a TypeScript module using the SDK to model a realistic sea turtle, roughly a meter in shell length, oriented along +Z, and thinking through how it should hold its height while gliding underwater off the ground.

I'm sketching the skeleton: a root hip joint at the shell's center, with spine chains extending forward toward the neck and backward toward the tail, so I can attach limbs and head naturally. For the shell geometry itself, I'm weighing options between extrusion, lathing, or lofting ellipse-like cross-sections along the body to get a convincing dome shape rather than a flat slab.

For the shell surface, I can paint plates using a scales pattern with olive and caramel base colors outlined in dark brown, which gives that cell-shaded, overlapping-plate look over a sphere's UV space. For the heart-shaped silhouette, I'm leaning toward building the shell with a loft instead of a plain sphere, varying the cross-section width per station so it's wide up front with a slight notch and narrows to a point at the back.

Still defining heart outline...

A flat heart plate reads more like a plate than a domed turtle shell, so I'm reconsidering giving the shell real volume underneath. I'll simplify by extruding the heart outline for the shell with moderate thickness and bevel, placing it at hip height above the body, rather than trying to layer a separate dome sphere underneath given time constraints.

I'll settle on a heart-shaped shell plate painted with scales as the main carapace, with a smaller dome ellipsoid underneath to add height at the center, sharing the same scale paint pattern so it reads as continuous shell.

For the neck and head, I'm planning a short thick turtle neck using a chain built from a three-point catmull path, which conveniently also yields a tip joint I can use as the head attachment point rather than needing a separate head joint.

I'm sizing the head as a scaled sphere flattened and elongated slightly for a blunt turtle shape, painted olive with cream-edged scales for that sea turtle look. For the eyes, I'm placing small dark spheres symmetrically on either side of the head front using left/forward/up offsets with a sign flip for mirroring, and I'm considering a gentle beak shape in dark olive or cream at the head's front tip.

Now I'm planning the front flippers as long, wide, flat limbs using a joint chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist to tip, and thinking through how to sweep or loft the shape so it tapers into a broad, flattened paddle rather than a rounded limb.

I'm working through the chain's roll orientation: setting up "up" as a vertical vector should put the normal pointing world-up, making the binormal span the fore-aft horizontal direction. That gives me rx as half the chord width and ry as half the thickness, which is exactly the flipper shape I want.

For the flipper chains themselves, I'm mirroring left and right by looping s across [1,-1], parenting each chain to the hips, and generating unique joint names per side (shoulder, elbow, wrist, flipTip) with role "arm". I'm laying out the actual 3D points for a wide front flipper using a catmull curve, then starting on a shorter rear flipper path near the hip.

For the rear legs, I'm defining a three-point hip-knee-foot chain with role "leg" and a tapered sweep radius, then adding a short stubby tail chain going backward from the hips with its own tapered radius.

Now I'm setting up the color palette — olive, caramel, dark brown, pale cream, and skin tones as hex strings — and thinking through how to add a pale underside belly plate using a scaled sphere positioned beneath the body for countershading.

I'm working out the geometry so the plastron (the belly plate) actually stays visible rather than getting swallowed by the body ellipsoid underneath it, adjusting the center heights and scale of both the body sphere and shell dome so they don't overlap awkwardly.

Now I'm trying to build the shell dome as a hemisphere sitting on the heart-shaped base plate, tuning the sphere geometry's phi/theta parameters and scale factors so the dome's footprint matches the heart outline without poking past the front lobes, and checking where the dome's flat base aligns with the plate's top surface.

For the plastron, I'm sketching a smaller rounded/heart outline slab positioned at y=0.6, under the shell perimeter so it's visible from below since I'm skipping a full body mesh, and considering how the flippers would attach near that same height.

Now I'm thinking about adding a remora fish riding under the shell's plastron, positioning its elongated tapered body around y=0.5-0.52 so it clears the plastron's bottom edge, sweeping it along a path with a tapered radius and giving it a sucking disc on its head as a distinguishing feature.

Still shaping the tail fin geometry...

For the head I'm scaling a sphere down to a small olive-and-cream shape positioned at the head joint tip, with a cream highlight sphere for the eye. For the neck, I'm building a curved chain from the hips through a notch in the shell front, using a catmull path with named joints ending in a tip that becomes the head's attachment point.

Now I'm sweeping the neck as a tapering skin-colored tube along that chain, and setting up the shell as a heart-shaped extrusion attached to the hips joint explicitly. For the flippers, I'm using an elliptical cross-section that tapers in width to create a flat, stylized paddle shape, with rounded caps and the chain parented to the hips.

I'm defining both front flipper chains (named by left/right side) and rear leg chains with tapering elliptical radii, plus placing a remora creature tucked under the shell near the hips. For coloring, I'm applying a scale-pattern paint using olive and caramel tones with adjustable size and width parameters.

Now I'm working out the head details: a horn-colored beak sphere scaled and oriented forward from the head bone, a blunted head shape with scales-pattern paint, and eye placements mirrored left and right using the head's local offset coordinates.

Settling on imports from the agentic-3js-builder module and deciding to type the outline arrays explicitly with OutlinePoint to keep things safe. Now defining the heart-shaped outline as a sequence of coordinate points with sharp corners marked at the top and bottom cusps...

Finishing the heart shape and moving to extrude it into a shell plate, working out thickness direction by cross-multiplying the outline's local axes so it sits centered along the correct axis. I'm positioning the dome, plastron, and remora fish/disc carefully so they overlap just enough to look attached rather than floating, adjusting heights by small increments until the gaps close up.

Now I'm laying out the neck, head, beak, and eye placements relative to a head joint using local offset vectors, then building the flipper and tail chains as catmull-spline paths with tapering radius functions for front limbs, hind limbs, and the tail. I'm also finalizing a palette of color constants for the shell, skin, beak, and remora, applying the scales paint function to the shell and head geometry, then assembling the full joint hierarchy under a root hips joint before writing out the final builder code.
